prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The intended answer is **block merge sort**, commonly implemented as **WikiSort** (also related to GrailSort).

It is a stable, in-place comparison sort with:

- **Worst-case time:** \(O(n \log n)\)
- **Best-case time:** \(O(n)\) on already sorted or nearly sorted data
- **Extra space:** \(O(1)\) in the strict in-place implementation

Ordinary **Timsort** also has \(O(n)\) best-case and \(O(n\log n)\) worst-case time, but it generally requires \(O(n)\) auxiliary space, so it is not strictly in-place.
